title: Idempotent requests
text: Idempotent requests Network failures happen. Send an Idempotency-Key header with every POST so that a retried request returns the original response instead of creating a second payment or refund. Use a random UUID per logical operation. Keys are remembered for 24 hours. Reusing a key with a different body returns 409 Conflict.

title: Accept a payment
text: Accept a payment Create a payment with POST /v1/payments. Send an idempotency key so that retries never charge a customer twice. Set amount in minor currency units: 2000 is $20.00. The currency must be usd, eur or gbp. Capture later To authorize now and capture when you ship, set capture to false, then call POST /v1/payments/{payment_id}/capture. Uncaptured payments are released after seven days. Check a payment Retrieve the latest state with GET /v1/payments/{payment_id}. The status is one of pending, succeeded, failed or refunded. To give money back, see partial refunds.

title: Refund a payment
text: Refund a payment Refunds return captured money to the customer. Create one with POST /v1/refunds. Full refunds Send only the payment_id. The full captured amount is refunded. Partial refunds Set amount (in minor units) to refund part of a payment. You can issue several partial refunds until the captured amount is used up. Field Required Notes payment_id yes The payment to refund amount no Defaults to the full captured amount reason no duplicate, fraudulent or requested_by_customer Note Need help? Email payments-support@acme.example.

title: Acme Payments
text: Acme Payments Acme Payments lets you accept card and bank payments and refund them. Task Guide Take a payment Accept a payment Give money back Refund a payment Retry safely Idempotent requests Find past payments GET /v1/payments returns payments, newest first All requests go to https://api.acme.example and authenticate with a secret API key sent as a bearer token. Note Need help? Email payments-support@acme.example.

title: Runbook: payment processor timeouts
text: Runbook: payment processor timeouts Use this runbook when the PaymentsProcessorTimeouts alert fires. Check the configuration Setting Default What it controls PAYMENTS_TIMEOUT_MS 30000 How long to wait for the card processor PAYMENTS_RETRY_LIMIT 3 Retries for idempotent processor calls Mitigate Check the processor status page. If p99 latency is above the timeout, raise PAYMENTS_TIMEOUT_MS temporarily and redeploy. If errors continue for more than 15 minutes, page the payments on-call engineer.

title: Create a payment
text: POST /v1/payments Create a payment Creates a payment. Set capture to false to authorize now and capture later. Parameters Header parameters Name Type Required Description Default / allowed values Idempotency-Key string optional Unique key that makes retries safe. Reusing a key returns the original response. Request body Required. Content type: application/json. Schema: PaymentCreate Request body (application/json) Name Type Required Description Default / allowed values amount integer required Amount in minor currency units (for example cents). Minimum: 50 currency string required Allowed: usd, eur, gbp customer_id string required description string optional capture boolean optional Capture immediately. Set to false to authorize only. Default: true Responses 201 Created Payment created.
